Pinn River School
Aims of our school
Aims of the school
At Pinn River School, we create a safe and welcoming learning community in which our pupils, families and staff contribute to creating a climate in which all are heard, understood and celebrated; enabling all to thrive, be challenged and achieve excellence.
The school aims to integrate education with therapy, providing a supportive environment that combines strong, multi-professional teams to enhance learning experiences.
Pinn River School is committed to offering a wide range of activities for pupils and their families, both after school and during holidays, to support social development and learning opportunities.
Roots of Respect
“Roots of Respect” is a child-centred framework created with the needs, voices, and lived experiences of our pupils at its heart, it aims to nurture a culture of empathy, dignity, and mutual understanding at Pinn River School.
Listen and Understand
Take time to listen and understand me at my own pace.
Clear Communication
Communicate in a way that suits my needs and helps me feel included.
Prepare Me for What’s Next
Let me know what’s going to happen and help me prepare.
Allow Choices
Give me time and space to make safe choices for myself.
Encourage My Voice
Listen to me regardless of how I communicate and encourage my voice.
Respect and Dignity
Treat me with respect and dignity at all times.
Stay Calm and Keep Me Safe
Remain calm even if I’m not, and help me feel safe.
Celebrate My Efforts
Praise my efforts and celebrate my achievements, however small.
Include Me
Talk to me, not about me, and keep me included in conversations.
Work Together
Support me in achieving my goals and inspire me to learn and shine.

Eden Academy Trust
The Eden Academy Trust
The Eden Academy Trust specialises in meeting the educational needs of children and young people with physical as well as moderate, severe and profound and multiple learning difficulties, including those with sensory impairment, ASD and emotional issues.
We are a family of schools who are working together under one Academy Trust, led by our Board of Trustees, to blend the best educational and therapeutic practice. Our team approach ensures we work closely with families and carers to identify and meet all the needs of our young people.
By working together, each school, every child and their family benefit from an enhanced range of provision, services and support including:
Take a look at the Eden Academy Trust website to find out more.
The Eden Academy Trust, company number 08036395, is registered in England & Wales at: The Eden Academy Trust (at Moorcroft School), Bramble Close, Uxbridge, England, UB8 3BF – email: info@theedenacademy.co.uk
Skilled and experienced staff

Pinn River School
Curriculum
Curriculum
Our curriculum at Pinn River School provides child led, motivating and relevant learning opportunities through a play-based approach/provision.
It is designed to help our learners thrive today and build happier, healthier futures.
• Communication – Pupils have a choice and a voice throughout the school day. Pupils learn to communicate using methods appropriate to their stage of development developing ownership of their own learning.
• Independence – Pupils are sensitively supported by highly skilled adults to actively participate in our school & wider community, at home and in their later lives. Pupils learn to anticipate, predict and participate in routines and healthy habits that enable them to develop independence.
• Active learning – Pupils learn through doing within real-life, motivating and engaging environments. In this play-based approach, pupils learn through exploring, discovering and investigating whilst developing social interaction skills. Staff are skilled at facilitating learning and modelling play approaches meeting each pupil ‘where they are at’ and enabling each pupil to experience a sense of achievement and sustain learning.
In order to meet all of our pupil’s needs, our curriculum is organised into four pathways.
Each pathway requires different teaching and learning approaches and environments with pupils working towards our pathway milestones.
Our three-year cycle ensures a breadth and balance of learning within each pathway.
If pupils are learning at a level where they can begin to access elements of the early National Curriculum, we extend their learning in line with their individual abilities in preparation for a transition to a new setting.
Our Early Learners Pathway provides our youngest pupils with a structured and motivating curriculum in a nurturing and secure environment where all pupils feel safe to explore our indoor and outdoor environments whilst learning through first hand experiences, regardless of their cognitive ability, physical or sensory need. Sessions are repeated across the week and term to encourage pupils to build routines, expectations and begin to anticipate learning and tasks.
Our Experience Learning Pathway is designed to expose pupils to early cognitive development that encourages engagement and understanding of themselves. Pupils will access an engaging early developmental, sensory and schema-based curriculum.
Our Explore Learning Pathway is for pupils with complex attention and interaction needs, who are unlikely to tolerate a ‘high demand’ approach to learning. Pupils will explore a highly motivating developmental, sensory and schema-based curriculum that supports regulation and builds engagement. Pupils begin to tolerate and accept others socially. Low demand play skills are developed and pupils are provided with opportunities to explore life skills to support them at home and in the community.
Our Engage Learning Pathway is for pupils who are ready to begin engaging in a wider range of learning areas, including understanding the world around them. Pupils at this stage engage in early, functional English and Mathematics whilst learning how to use their communication method across the school day. Expressive subjects provide an environment for pupils to consolidate foundation skills whilst further developing play skills in real-life contexts. Pupils are provided with opportunities to explore life skills to support them at home and in the community.
As well as offering a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum, we believe that the links between language development and cognition advancement are the key drivers in ensuring progress and improvement.
Teaching and learning opportunities
We believe that all the experiences that a pupil encounters, from their arrival at school to the time they leave each day, present teaching and learning opportunities.
The curriculum at Pinn River School is therefore not just classroom-bound, but is the foundation of all that we do to provide capitalising upon these learning opportunities and making them accessible, manageable and of worth for each pupil. It is reflected in the school environment, the conduct and values of all staff and the carefully-planned and sensitive support we provide.
Learning takes place all over the school site and in the local community, using classrooms as a secure base for pupils, traditional teacher-led sessions and social group-work. Further opportunities are found in the routines of transition times, break-times and times of self-care.
Find out more about our curriculum principles, framework and guidance and our termly subject overviews here.
Pinn River Careers Policy
Pinn River Career Statement
Learning Themes
At Pinn River School, the curriculum is delivered through whole school themes for each term that are broken down into themes related to each Key Stage. Whole school themes are enhanced further through our core and expressive subject areas, adapted to meet the learner characteristic for pupils accessing different learner pathways, ensuring interventions and therapies are integrated throughout the day.
As these themes follow a three-year cycle, each pupil will experience most whole school themes twice within the context of each key stage theme. Year 6 pupils are given the opportunity to consolidate and expand their learning through revisiting the theme they experienced in Year 3 with greater depth.
Themes provide pupils with a variety of experiences throughout their time at Pinn River School, whilst they work towards their own individual goals. Therefore, learners who need to spend a number of years developing a specific skill can still experience this through a variety of mediums.
Resources are also sourced that relate to each term’s theme, providing teachers with a bank of diverse curriculum resources, thus providing pupils with broad and balanced learning opportunities as they progress through each key stage.
Communication
All our pupils different needs are assessed using 6 communication bandings and we deliver our curriculum to match them.
Right to Withdraw from Religious Education (RE)
Parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education. This right can be exercised at any time and does not require a reason.
If you are considering withdrawal and would like to discuss this further, or to understand how RE is taught at Pinn River School, please contact the school so we can talk through the options with you.

Pinn River School
Family Services
Your Family Support Coordinators
Lindsey Gregory and Shriti Thompson are the Pinn River School’s Family Services Coordinators.
Our role in school is to provide support, advice and information to the families within our school community.
We can help you with any worries you may have concerning your child’s education, behaviour and wellbeing. We are also here to support parents with issues that may be impacting their family such as health or finances.
Advice and support are confidential, although concerns relating to safeguarding children will always be dealt with as per the school’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy.
We are also here as someone to talk to if you need it. We may not have all the answers, but hopefully we can help you to work out how to find them.
This may be achieved through 1:1s or small group support. We also are very pleased to be supported by DASH a local charity for people with disabilities.
Emotional, practical and social support
Eden’s centralised Family Service team provide links between home, school and other services, to strengthen relationships and communication.
They work individually with families who need support, advice or guidance about statutory services involvement and those who are finding it difficult to manage their child’s behaviour or needs at home.
They also provide pupils and their families with a range of activities outside school hours so both pupils and their sibling and families have opportunities to socialise and have experiences otherwise inaccessible to them.

We are based in school and can meet with you at school, at home, or even at a local coffee shop; we can meet at a time that works for each of us. You can get in touch by calling the school office on 01895 808 776

Pinn River School
Governance & Local Advisory Board
Governance is a system of rules, practices and processes by which the Eden Academy Trust and each of the schools are managed.
Governance across the Trust has been established to support our vision:
The Eden Academy Trust will create centres of educational excellence where our young people will achieve exceptional outcomes
Governance at the Eden Academy Trust is led by the following:
The Board of Members
The Board of Members (or ‘members’) has ultimate control over the Eden Academy Trust.
They have the power to:
Members meet once a year for an Annual General Meeting where they review performance across the Trust as well as discuss with Trustees new developments and their vision for the future. You can find more information and profiles of the members here.
Review the Declarations of Interest of the Eden Academy Trust Members, Trustees and Audit Committee Members.
appoint (or remove) Trustees
The Board of Trustees Committees
Pinn River School Local Advisory Board
The Pinn River School Local Advisory Board (LAB) is a group of parents, staff and community representatives who provide advice and support to help the school achieve its aims. The LAB is not a legal entity in its own right. Legal accountability for all aspects of the school lies with the Trustees including finance, personnel and premises, and the educational performance of the school.
The LAB is designed to help key stakeholders to get involved in the life of the school and the Trust, contribute to its development and promote the school within the community. Individual members of the LAB can be invited to be part of a Board of Trustees Committee.
The LAB meets three times a year but LAB members may also set up their own groups to focus on specific areas which might meet more frequently and include regular visits to the school.
Read more about the LAB at Pinn River School here.
The Board of Trustees
The Board of Trustees (or ‘trustees’) are responsible for the performance, achievement and overall direction of the Eden Academy Trust. Legal accountability for all aspects of the Trust lies with the trustees including finance, personnel and premises, and the educational performance of the schools.
The trustees offer support, constructive advice and help to the CEO, Senior Leadership team and School Heads where needed, but will also challenge, ask questions and seek information to find the best solution for the Trust.

Pinn River School
How we learn
How we learn
Pinn River School is designed to meet the needs of our pupils and to promote a sense of belonging.
Pupils learn in one of four key-stage learning communities/hubs. These are a secure base for teacher directed sessions and social group-work.
Organisation of these learning communities helps to ensure that all pupils receive an appropriate balance of whole class, small group, and individual teaching.
Each key-stage community has flexible workrooms for 1:1 and small group work to enable pupils to move with ease between learning sessions and therapeutic sessions therefore enabling independence.
Each learning community has its own large communal space and access to shared, secure outdoor areas to encourage social interaction.
We build honest working relationships with our parents and staff. Our school is a real community; the doors are always open.
